title: Knee Arthroscopy for Meniscal Tears (Synthetic Health Plan — fictional policy)

sections.title: Synthetic Content Notice
sections.text: This document is a SYNTHETIC, fictional medical policy written for software testing and demonstration. It is not issued by any real health plan and must not be used for real coverage decisions.

sections.title: Coverage Criteria
sections.text:
Arthroscopic partial meniscectomy or meniscal repair of the knee is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:

1. The member reports mechanical symptoms of the knee, such as locking, catching, or giving way, documented in the clinical record.
2. The member has completed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy within the past 12 months, including physical therapy or a supervised home exercise program, AND at least one of: oral anti-inflammatory medication, activity modification, or bracing, unless contraindicated.
3. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) performed within the past 6 months demonstrates a meniscal tear that correlates with the clinical findings.
4. Radiographs do not demonstrate advanced osteoarthritis of the affected compartment (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4).
5. A functional limitation attributable to the knee is documented, such as difficulty with stairs, ambulation, or work duties, using a validated score where available (for example, a KOOS or IKDC score).

The requirement for 6 weeks of conservative therapy does not apply when there is a locked knee that cannot be reduced, or an acute traumatic tear with a displaced bucket-handle fragment confirmed on MRI.

sections.title: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:
Arthroscopic lavage and/or debridement as a treatment for osteoarthritis of the knee without mechanical symptoms is not medically necessary.

Arthroscopic meniscectomy is not medically necessary for degenerative meniscal tears in members with advanced osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4) of the same compartment.

Diagnostic arthroscopy alone is not medically necessary when MRI findings are sufficient to establish the diagnosis.

sections.title: Documentation Requirements
sections.text:
The following documentation must accompany the prior authorization request:

- Office notes from the treating clinician dated within the past 60 days describing the mechanical symptoms and examination findings (for example, joint line tenderness, a positive McMurray test).
- Dates and outcomes of conservative therapy, including physical therapy visit dates or a home exercise log.
- The MRI report, including the date of the study and the interpretation of the meniscal tear.
- Radiograph report describing the degree of osteoarthritis in the affected compartment.
- The documented functional limitation, including any validated outcome score.

sections.title: Applicable Codes
sections.text:
Procedure codes: 29880, 29881, 29882, 29883 (knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy or meniscal repair).
Supporting diagnosis codes include: M23.2 (derangement of meniscus due to old tear or injury) and its subcodes; S83.2 (tear of meniscus, current injury) and its subcodes.
Non-supporting diagnosis codes when billed alone: M17.0, M17.11, M17.12 (primary osteoarthritis of knee).
